1: //! Generic recursive counting and folding over sequences.
2: //!
3: //! Provides a generic `count_matching` spec and proof that the count is
4: //! bounded by the sequence length. This eliminates duplicate inductive
5: //! proofs across `collections`, `env_scrub`, `approval`, and `eviction`.
6: 
7: use vstd::prelude::*;
8: 
9: verus! {
10: 
11: // ============================================================
12: // Generic count_matching: count elements satisfying a predicate
13: // ============================================================
14: 
15: // r[depends seq-fold.count-matching]
16: /// Spec: number of elements in `s[from..]` satisfying predicate `p`.
17: pub open spec fn count_matching_from_spec(
18:     s: Seq<u64>, p: spec_fn(u64) -> bool, from: int,
19: ) -> nat
20:     decreases s.len() - from,
21: {
22:     if from < 0 || from >= s.len() {
23:         0
24:     } else if p(s[from]) {
25:         1 + count_matching_from_spec(s, p, from + 1)
26:     } else {
27:         count_matching_from_spec(s, p, from + 1)
28:     }
29: }
30: 
31: // r[depends seq-fold.count-matching]
32: /// Spec: total count of elements satisfying predicate `p`.
33: pub open spec fn count_matching_spec(
34:     s: Seq<u64>, p: spec_fn(u64) -> bool,
35: ) -> nat {
36:     count_matching_from_spec(s, p, 0)
37: }
38: 
39: // ============================================================
40: // Bounded count lemma
41: // ============================================================
42: 
43: // r[verify seq-fold.count-matching]
44: /// Count from any position is bounded by remaining length.
45: pub proof fn count_matching_from_bounded(
46:     s: Seq<u64>, p: spec_fn(u64) -> bool, from: int,
47: )
48:     requires 0 <= from <= s.len()
49:     ensures count_matching_from_spec(s, p, from) as int <= s.len() - from
50:     decreases s.len() - from,
51: {
52:     if from < s.len() {
53:         count_matching_from_bounded(s, p, from + 1);
54:     }
55: }
56: 
57: // r[verify seq-fold.count-matching]
58: /// Total count is bounded by sequence length.
59: pub proof fn count_matching_bounded(
60:     s: Seq<u64>, p: spec_fn(u64) -> bool,
61: )
62:     ensures count_matching_spec(s, p) as int <= s.len()
63: {
64:     count_matching_from_bounded(s, p, 0);
65: }
66: 
67: // r[verify seq-fold.count-matching]
68: /// Empty sequence has zero count.
69: pub proof fn count_matching_empty(p: spec_fn(u64) -> bool)
70:     ensures count_matching_spec(Seq::<u64>::empty(), p) == 0
71: {}
72: 
73: // ============================================================
74: // All-matching lemma
75: // ============================================================
76: 
77: // r[verify seq-fold.count-matching]
78: /// If every element satisfies `p`, count equals length.
79: pub proof fn count_matching_all(
80:     s: Seq<u64>, p: spec_fn(u64) -> bool,
81: )
82:     requires forall|i: int| 0 <= i < s.len() ==> p(s[i])
83:     ensures count_matching_spec(s, p) == s.len()
84: {
85:     count_matching_all_from(s, p, 0);
86: }
87: 
88: /// Helper: if all elements from `from` onward satisfy `p`, count = remaining.
89: proof fn count_matching_all_from(
90:     s: Seq<u64>, p: spec_fn(u64) -> bool, from: int,
91: )
92:     requires
93:         0 <= from <= s.len(),
94:         forall|i: int| from <= i < s.len() ==> p(s[i]),
95:     ensures count_matching_from_spec(s, p, from) as int == s.len() - from
96:     decreases s.len() - from,
97: {
98:     // Repair only this body. Prove the unchanged postcondition.
99: }
100: 
101: // ============================================================
102: // None-matching lemma
103: // ============================================================
104: 
105: // r[verify seq-fold.count-matching]
106: /// If no element satisfies `p`, count is zero.
107: pub proof fn count_matching_none(
108:     s: Seq<u64>, p: spec_fn(u64) -> bool,
109: )
110:     requires forall|i: int| 0 <= i < s.len() ==> !p(s[i])
111:     ensures count_matching_spec(s, p) == 0
112: {
113:     count_matching_none_from(s, p, 0);
114: }
115: 
116: /// Helper: no matching elements from `from` onward.
117: proof fn count_matching_none_from(
118:     s: Seq<u64>, p: spec_fn(u64) -> bool, from: int,
119: )
120:     requires
121:         0 <= from <= s.len(),
122:         forall|i: int| from <= i < s.len() ==> !p(s[i]),
123:     ensures count_matching_from_spec(s, p, from) == 0
124:     decreases s.len() - from,
125: {
126:     if from < s.len() {
127:         count_matching_none_from(s, p, from + 1);
128:     }
129: }
130:
